vcc_submit.note: Final-phase scores stay hidden until the winners are announced, so no score is recorded here.

provenance_note: Assembled by hand from logs/build-submission.log, logs/prep.log and logs/submit.log,
not written by scripts/20 as usual: the machine lost power during that run's `vcc prep`
step, after the .h5ad had been written and verified complete. `vcc prep` was then re-run
standalone on that same .h5ad, which is also the lower-memory path (no parent process
holding the control matrices). The shrinkage figures are as scripts/20 printed them, to
three decimal places; re-running `python scripts/20_make_vcc_submission.py --method mean`
reproduces them exactly, since the pipeline is seeded (seed 0).
RETRACTED: an earlier version of this record said prep_peak_gib (vcc/sizing.py)
under-predicted this run -- ~21.3 GiB predicted against ~31 GB actual -- and blamed the
gap on the input being gzip-compressed internally. That was wrong. The 31 GB was the
machine's system-wide commit charge, which counts every other process on it; prep's own
peak was never measured. Re-measured since, on a 60,000-cell slice of this same file
(331,761,889 stored entries, `vcc prep --dry-run`, peak working set over the process
tree -- the matrix is held by a grandchild python.exe, not the vcc.exe stub): 5.06 GiB
actual against the model's 5.21 GiB, the same to the hundredth of a GiB whether the
input was gzip-compressed (0.63 GiB on disk) or uncompressed (2.48 GiB). Compression
changed the runtime, 17s against 8s, and not the memory. Scaled to this file's
1,989,779,692 entries, the measured 1.24x-the-matrix slope puts the real peak near
20 GiB. The model is accurate and slightly conservative, as its own docstring intends.
